claims.text: Incorporating approximately 5 at.% Al into a BCC NbMoTaW-based refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Approximately 5 at.% Al will promote formation of a continuous α-Al2O3 surface scale.
The α-Al2O3 scale will adhere to the alloy surface.
The α-Al2O3 scale will slow oxidation.
As-cast or arc-melted refractory high-entropy alloys are typically single-phase BCC materials.
The untreated alloy rapidly oxidizes and undergoes oxide-scale spallation at extreme temperatures in air.
Al is to be incorporated during processing, for example by vacuum arc melting.
The proposed performance test uses air containing 21% O2 at 1100 °C for 100 hours.
A continuous α-Al2O3 scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen and metal ions.
Al has a high affinity for oxygen.
Al in the refractory high-entropy alloy preferentially oxidizes during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential oxidation of Al forms a dense α-Al2O3 layer.
The alumina layer reduces oxygen ingress and oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will have a lower oxidation rate than the untreated alloy at 1100 °C in air.
The Al-modified alloy may show a 50–70% reduction in oxidation-associated weight gain over 100 hours.
The untreated alloy forms a non-uniform, poorly protective oxide scale that spalls and produces higher oxidation rates and weight gain.
The protective effect is expected between approximately 1000 °C and 1200 °C in standard air.
Significantly higher temperatures or high water-vapor content may compromise α-Al2O3 stability or adherence.
The magnitude of oxidation improvement may depend on alloy composition, processing history, and test conditions.
Interactions between Al and other refractory elements may affect scale-formation kinetics and adherence.
